requirements.requirement: A persistent host firewall (firewalld) is enabled on node1, active at runtime and enabled/persisted across boot
requirements.summary: firewalld was already active; executor confirmed it is enabled at boot (systemctl is-enabled firewalld -> enabled) both before and after a real reboot, with --permanent config matching runtime config.

Permanent and runtime zone config list 'services: ssh'; nft filter_IN_public_allow explicitly accepts tcp dport 22; SSH remained reachable throughout (executor never lost connectivity except during the reboot window itself).

Permanent and runtime config list 'ports: 8080/tcp'; nft filter_IN_public_allow explicitly accepts tcp dport 8080; a live HTTP listener on 8080 was reachable (curl 200 OK) both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Unrelated inbound connections are rejected, not merely default-accepted
requirements.summary: nft ruleset shows the public zone chain falls through to 'reject with icmpx admin-prohibited' for anything not explicitly allowed; a live functional test against unrelated port 9999 returned connection-refused (curl exit 7) both before and after reboot. Pre-existing stray allowances (cockpit, dhcpv6-client) were removed so only ssh/8080 remain permitted.

requirements.requirement: Firewall configuration and required services survive a reboot (persistent, not just runtime-applied)
requirements.summary: A full pre-restart baseline (boot_id, firewalld active/enabled, sshd active), a genuine restart (boot_id changed from 8c28f3cd... to 74e3d244..., corroborated independently by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots), and post-restart recovery (identical persisted zone rules, firewalld active/enabled, sshd active, and identical 8080-allow/9999-reject functional behavior) were all directly observed.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: firewalld is persistently enabled on node1 with only ssh and 8080/tcp permitted, unrelated traffic is explicitly rejected (verified via nft rules and live functional tests, not just default policy), and the configuration and functional behavior survived a genuine, independently corroborated reboot (boot_id change). Hygiene is good; the only configuration mutation was task-required, temporary test listeners were cleaned up, and only a few harmless log files were left behind.
limitations: A brief command (cmd-6e7a079be5e642b0) failed due to a missing 'nc' binary before the executor switched to curl-based functional tests; this had no effect on the outcome but slightly reduces trace tidiness.
Minor log-file residue (/tmp/http8080.log, /tmp/http8080b.log, /tmp/reboot.log) remained after the run; low risk but not cleaned up.
Prepare phase was disabled (after_prepare is an alias of before_prepare), so the before/after-prepare distinction was not meaningfully exercised; all changes are attributable to the executor.

operational_hygiene.summary: The one state-changing configuration action (cmd-a700f9b93f0743dd) was directly required by the task: it removed pre-existing stray permanent service allowances (cockpit, dhcpv6-client) and added the required ssh/8080 rules, which is exactly what 'reject unrelated inbound' demands. The two temporary HTTP listeners used for functional testing (cmd-e1b80336d0a44872, cmd-63044cb380954aae) were bounded and self-terminated (cmd-521923350863429f and an inline pkill in cmd-63044cb380954aae), leaving no listening socket residue (confirmed by cmd-2ae832fc98d744de and the after-executor listening-sockets snapshot showing only sshd/chronyd). The reboot trigger (cmd-dfb7ba79e6f54681) was a necessary prerequisite for the mandated restart-evidence protocol. Minor residue: three log files (/tmp/http8080.log, /tmp/http8080b.log, /tmp/reboot.log) from the test listeners and the backgrounded reboot command were left in /tmp per the after-executor temporary-files snapshot; these are low-risk, non-sensitive artifacts and were not cleaned up. One command (cmd-6e7a079be5e642b0) failed because 'nc' was not installed and caused no state change. No failed services, no weakened security posture, no package damage observed.
